fit: oral ground C.verum and movement outcomes after acute MPTP in mice
assessment: Ground cinnamon started three hours after MPTP and favored seven-day rotarod and open-field movement versus vehicle; Figure8 gives six mice/group. This early post-insult motor signal supports a limited favorable bridge without a clinical gait-speed estimate. Benzoate was a separate arm.

fit: acute oral solvent-extracted walnut oil and recorded tolerability
assessment: The component crossover reports nonsystematically collected diarrhea in9/15 oil recipients versus0/15 each other component during0–360minutes. No separate pain-coded event is reported; thresholdzero is not proof that pain was absent. Fifty-one grams solvent-extracted oil is not a chronic cold-pressed Parkinson pain comparison.

fit: uncontrolled advanced-cancer diet offering a walnut-containing mixed-oil shake
assessment: Sixteen enrolled,five completed and seven had evaluable quality-of-life trajectories. Pain increased during advanced cancer progression; insomnia improved. Table3 lists walnut among seven shake oils. Individual oil intake and processing are unverified. Preserve the unfavorable pain trajectory without attributing it to an isolated oil.

fit: commercial walnut hydrosol in an uncontrolled insulin-treated diabetes pilot
assessment: Eight participants received hydrosol alongside insulin; two rashes and one hypoglycemic coma occurred. Authors considered the coma probably related, but this design cannot establish causation. Product plant part and processing are unverified; separately analyzed volatile fraction is not the administered pressed oil. No pain or Parkinson comparison.

fit: locally injected immature green-walnut fruit extract in mouse pain assays
assessment: Groups of six had favorable induced thermal and formalin nociception results, while edema reduction was inconclusive. Whole immature-fruit hydroethanolic extract and local injection differ from consumed kernel oil. This adds a preclinical plant-material lead rather than another whole-oil or human pain trial.

fit: planned advanced-cancer symptom comparison using a mixed oil placebo
assessment: Current registration lists cold-pressed walnut oil among placebo ingredients and plans individual ESAS symptoms including pain. Matched protocol is the same trial but does not name the oil ingredients. Results, exposure history and any isolated oil effect remain unverified; earlier MedCan formulations are distinct.
